summary: nitro-bundled-dep posts host identity to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The npm package nitro-bundled-dep@0.0.1 presents itself as a 'Compatibility shim' but ships a beacon that POSTs installer host metadata — hostname, install path, current working directory, and Node version — to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon in beacon.cjs is invoked from package.json's postinstall script, so it fires automatically on `npm install`, and is also invoked from index.js so it fires again whenever the module is required. The main module exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, allowing a victim build that imports this name to continue without errors after the beacon has executed — the shape of a dependency-confusion / name-squat payload whose purpose is to confirm successful code execution inside a target build environment and report host identifiers to an attacker-controlled collector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
